clusters.label: Thermogalvanic effect
clusters.definition: Temperature-dependent electrochemical redox behavior that produces an electrical response to heat.
clusters.reason: All denote the thermogalvanic process. Redox species, matrices, enhancement mechanisms and applications qualify individual claims; thermodiffusion and other coupled effects remain distinct.

clusters.label: Power generation
clusters.definition: Production of electrical power by a thermogalvanic cell.
clusters.reason: Both explicitly describe electrical power generation; device composition and operating context differ without changing this function.

clusters.label: Low thermal conductivity
clusters.definition: A low ability to conduct heat.
clusters.reason: All describe low thermal conductivity itself, rather than a reduction or electrical conductivity. Material identities remain attached to their claims.

clusters.label: KCl
clusters.reason: The explicit chemical composition is identical; ion provision and complexation are different contextual roles of the same compound.

clusters.label: Ion diffusion
clusters.reason: Both denote ion diffusion. Improvement and reduction are opposite effects on that process, preserved in the respective relations.

clusters.label: Redox reactions
clusters.definition: Oxidation and reduction reactions involving electron transfer.
clusters.reason: Both labels denote the general reaction class; the evidence supplies different promoting mechanisms without naming different reaction subtypes.

unresolved.reason: Conductivity type is unspecified; the electrode's electrical, photothermal and heat-storage context does not resolve it.
Conductivity type is explicitly unspecified, preventing a defensible identification of the quantity or equivalence.

clusters.label: Anti-freezing properties
clusters.definition: Ability to resist freezing under low-temperature conditions.
clusters.reason: Both describe freezing resistance of DMSO/water organohydrogels; hydrogen bonding is a supporting mechanism, not a different property.

clusters.label: Excellent mechanical stability
clusters.definition: Strong retention of mechanical integrity or behavior.
clusters.reason: Both denote mechanical stability. The tensile cycling condition is specific to the hydrogel claim and does not redefine the shared property.

clusters.label: Electrical conductivity
clusters.definition: The physical quantity describing a material's ability to conduct electric current.
clusters.reason: Both explicitly name electrical conductivity; neither names a carrier-specific subtype. Improvement remains a relation on the quantity.

clusters.label: Gel-based thermogalvanic cell (P0057)
clusters.definition: The study's thermogalvanic cell using the PVA/gelation hydrogel electrolyte identified in its title.
clusters.reason: The title and reported output identify a particular study device; no evidence establishes identity with the other cell.

clusters.label: Gel-based thermogalvanic cell (P0068)
clusters.definition: The study's thermogalvanic hydrogel cell used for temperature monitoring of edibles.
clusters.reason: The label refers to the particular sensor cell whose outputs are reported, rather than establishing a shared material class or device identity.

clusters.label: High transparency
clusters.definition: A high degree of optical transparency.
clusters.reason: Both describe the same optical property; polymer networks, redox species and preparation mechanisms remain claim-specific.

clusters.label: Seebeck effect
clusters.definition: Generation of an electrical potential difference in response to a temperature difference in thermogalvanic cells.
clusters.reason: Both concern the Seebeck response in thermogalvanic cells; Soret coupling and redox-entropy enhancement describe influences on that response.

clusters.label: PEDOT:PSS
clusters.reason: The same explicitly named polymer material appears as a hydrogel component and a reviewed thermoelectric platform.

clusters.label: Stretchability
clusters.definition: Ability of a material or device to undergo tensile extension.
clusters.reason: All denote the same mechanical capability; compositions, device geometries and fabrication methods qualify separate claims.

clusters.label: Self-powered body temperature monitoring
clusters.definition: Monitoring human body temperature using a sensing system that supplies its own operating power.
clusters.reason: Both explicitly describe the same application; wrist and forehead placement are implementation conditions.

unresolved.reason: “Moderate” thermoelectric performance has no specified metric or benchmark, so a well-defined performance concept cannot be established.
The qualitative assessment covers both positive- and negative-Seebeck gels without defining a performance metric or benchmark.

clusters.label: Output voltage
clusters.definition: Electrical potential difference delivered at a device's output.
clusters.reason: Both denote output voltage itself; correlation with light intensity and amplification are distinct relations on this quantity.

clusters.label: Water solubility
clusters.definition: Ability of a substance to dissolve in water.
clusters.reason: Both explicitly describe water solubility. Oxidation state and chemical identity belong to the respective substances, not different solubility concepts.

unresolved.reason: The evidence reports thermopower but does not define the broader performance enhancement or its comparison baseline sufficiently to identify a specific outcome concept.
A proposed general performance enhancement is given without a metric; it cannot be equated with an observed thermogalvanic outcome.
“Giant thermoelectric performance” and increased hybrid entropy do not specify which performance quantity is enhanced or by what comparison.
